scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions and comments. Focus: relevance, nDCG, CTR, query understanding, retrieval and ranking.

papers.title: Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents
papers.authors: Chenxi Li, Xueyang Feng, Songyang Liu, Chenxu Wang, Xiaoying Tang, Chaozhuo Li, Litian Zhang
papers.summary: The method calibrates on-policy distillation with information gained after retrieval, adjusting both turn-level supervision and query preferences. The 2B student gains 3.4 accuracy points on average across six multimodal search benchmarks.
papers.key_insight: Train against what a query retrieves, rather than its appearance to the teacher. Token volume can underweight short but informative search turns.

papers.title: Retrieved but Not Read: Understanding Why Search-Augmented LLMs Fail to Use Available Evidence
papers.authors: Owen Walters, Lihu Chen, Francesca Toni
papers.summary: The study separates finding current evidence from using it in the final answer. Across six open-weight configurations and a proprietary deployment, models sometimes rely on snippets and retain stale answers despite available evidence.
papers.key_insight: Track evidence discovery, page opening and final answer use separately. Better retrieval alone may leave a stale-answer failure unresolved.

papers.title: TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Tanish Kher, Sarvesh DK, Abedelkadir Asi, Sparsha Chennarayapatna Sundaresh, Dezhi Hong
papers.summary: TRACER indexes observed tool-call sequences in a trie and combines empirical and contextual priors to rank continuations. In a mixed retail and telecom setting, tool-selection accuracy improves by 4.7 points.
papers.key_insight: Use action history as retrieval context. Measure coverage of rare trajectories as well as average selection accuracy when shrinking the candidate registry.

papers.title: SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Giancarlo Maldonado Cárdenas, Carlos A. Astudillo, Nelson L. S. da Fonseca
papers.summary: SSR uses structural lexical signals from Agent Cards and an inverted index to preselect agents without training. At 1,000 agents, orchestration latency falls by 70.9% relative to passing the complete catalog.
papers.key_insight: Field structure can make lexical retrieval useful before orchestration. The evidence concerns capability matching, rather than relevance ranking of community posts.

papers.title: GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models
papers.authors: Weiting Liu, Zhiyu Pan, Shuhong Wang, Zhenquan Yao, Jungang Li, Li Zhao, Jian Jiang, Jianfeng Feng, Ai Han, Wenlian Lu
papers.summary: GACC-Bench tests whether compressed context preserves information for a goal before the exact questions are known. It contains 500 goals. Goal conditioning helps, but even the best tested compressor falls short of full context.
papers.key_insight: Evaluate compression against several withheld questions per goal. A good answer to one question can hide the loss of other relevant details.

papers.title: CARA: Causally Guided Retrieval Agent for Question Answering
papers.authors: Weicheng Liu, Xiangcheng Wu, Depeng Xu, Haopeng Zhang, Xi Niu
papers.summary: CARA evaluates evidence through addition and removal tests, then combines these signals with path consistency for graph exploration. It is tested on three STaRK datasets; the abstract does not give a single aggregate improvement.
papers.key_insight: Test whether evidence changes answerability rather than treating semantic similarity as utility. Account for the extra evaluation calls when measuring retrieval cost.
